reviews.reason: Direct queen fork restores a minor-piece deficit while an advanced passed pawn keeps real counterplay; all four legal king replies lose the bishop. The fork, rather than a routine capture, creates the gain.
reviews.distinctness: Unlike the existing Dubois and Baklan queen/bishop examples with interposition replies, this position requires a queen square attacking a bishop on a separate file while retaining a6-pawn counterplay. All defences are king moves. Qc6+ and Qc8+ are equivalent fork routes, not extra exercises; the played Qc6+ route is explicitly distinguished from the Qb5+ sample.
reviews.solutionVi: Qb5+ chiếu Vua e8, đồng thời tấn công Tượng c5. Sau Kf7, Qxc5 thu Tượng; các nước Vua khác cũng không cứu được Tượng. Đây là phương án minh họa. Trong ván gốc, Trắng chọn Qc6+ rồi Qxc5.
hintsVi: Tìm nước chiếu của Hậu đồng thời tấn công Tượng c5.
So sánh các ô chiếu trên cột b và cột c; đừng vội bắt Tốt d5.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White starts 330 cp down in nominal material. Qb5+ attacks king e8 and bishop c5 (also pawn c4), so the king must move and Qxc5 gains the bishop. The bishop was not attacked by Qb7. The important a6 passer and Black queen/minors create meaningful contest, not an already unopposed material collection.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Compared all 35 legal roots. No immediate safe gain or mate. Qxd5? exd5 loses the queen; b4 is only about equality in the bounded root search, not a short guaranteed gain. Qc6+ (actually played) and Qc8+ also create the same king/bishop fork, and must not be called incorrect. No non-fork two-solver-move material shortcut was verified or unresolved.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All four legal replies Kf8,Kd8,Kf7,Ke7 permit Qxc5, surviving every immediate countercapture. Strong search includes Kf7 Qxc5 Qxb2 and c3 alternatives; Black can recover a pawn or pursue activity, but cannot recover the whole bishop or refute the material gain in the reviewed lines. No sacrifice offers in preflight. Do not call Kf7 forced.
reviewNotes.level: A: two solver moves, an immediate checking queen fork followed by the target capture, without a preparatory sacrifice. Passed-pawn consequences are context, not required extra solution moves.
reviewNotes.provenance: Exact complete TWIC1664 game replay, source FEN, preceding move, headers, archive sha256 and source ply match. TWIC headers identify White as IM Arab,A (FIDE7900872). Independently verified IM Arab Adlane7900872 in the FIDE-hosted 2019 African Games report, PDF p8 and p10: https://pdc.fide.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Morocco_final.pdf . Qb5+ is teaching analysis; game played Qc6+ Kd8 Qxc5.

reviews.reason: Balanced-material position where the direct knight fork wins the exchange despite a legal pawn recapture. The copy states the net exchange gain, not a free rook.
reviews.distinctness: Related to existing knight/king/rook forks, but the concrete recovery decision is a d-pawn recapture that leaves connected Black passed pawns and active rooks; the learner must count the exchange rather than claim a whole rook. Unlike the nearby Simon Ne5+ pawn fork, the c4 rook is defended and the published material explanation includes dxc4. The active counterplay and initially equal material justify this selected related example.
reviews.solutionVi: Ne5+ đưa Mã từ f3 đến e5, chiếu Vua f7 và tấn công Xe c4. Sau Ke6, Nxc4 thắng chất: đổi Mã lấy Xe. Đen có thể bắt lại bằng dxc4, nhưng Trắng vẫn thu lợi về vật chất.
hintsVi: Tìm nước chiếu của Mã đồng thời tấn công một Xe.
Sau khi bắt Xe c4, hãy tính cả khả năng Tốt d5 bắt lại Mã.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Initial nominal material is equal. Ne5+ creates the king-f7/rook-c4 fork, forcing the king to answer before the rook can escape. Nxc4 remains a favorable knight-for-rook exchange after dxc4. The rook is not already attacked by the f3 knight; the checking fork creates the opportunity.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 34 legal roots compared; no immediate mate, safe free capture or verified two-move non-fork material shortcut. Rxd5 gives Black Rxc2 and continued counterplay rather than a simpler clean pawn gain; its engine line needs further rook manoeuvres. Ra6 similarly allows Rxd5/Rxc2 exchanges. Neither gives a clearly superior payoff at no greater difficulty. Ne5+ is the strongest compared root.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Every one of the six legal king replies Kg8,Ke8,Kg7,Ke7,Kf6,Ke6 permits Nxc4 and at least a net exchange gain after any immediate reply. Relevant dxc4 is explicitly acknowledged; the sample capture is not a five-point net gain. Strong lines continue through dxc4 and active passed-pawn/rook counterplay with retained positive evaluation. Ke7 can also allow the longer Ng6+ fork route, but is not required. No offered sacrifice before the fork.
reviewNotes.level: A: direct knight check and immediate fork capture, two solver moves. Trading the lower-value knight for the rook is a favorable exchange, not a preparatory sacrifice. Copy exposes the obvious pawn recapture so the short line is not misrepresented.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete original TWIC1664 game, exact FEN, preceding move and legal source ply checked; Ne5+ Ke6 Nxc4 dxc4 was actually played. Official FIDE profile https://ratings.fide.com/profile/10105972 identifies Junior, Domingos (10105972) as FIDE Master since2017, matching the archive identity and pre-2026 title requirement. Archive sha256/retrieval metadata retained.

reviews.reason: Queen fork wins a knight with tempo while White faces concrete king-side threats. All legal checking replies are covered, including an immediate mate after the inferior king retreat.
reviews.distinctness: Adds a defensive use of the fork: White must retain forcing play in front of its exposed king against queen/rook threats. Capturing d7 directly with the rook fails to the king recapture, while the queen reaches d7 with check and support from Rd1. The Kd8 defence permits immediate mate; the best Kb7 defence leaves an active Rc7 resource. This differs from the existing Mongredien queen/knight fork, where Black has additional pieces and a promoted-pawn threat rather than White using a fork to maintain forcing defence.
reviews.solutionVi: Qd6+ chiếu Vua c7, đồng thời tấn công Mã d7. Sau Kb7, Qxd7+ thu Mã và tiếp tục chiếu; Xe d1 bảo vệ Hậu. Nếu Đen chọn Kd8 thì Qxd7# chiếu hết.
hintsVi: Tìm nước chiếu của Hậu đồng thời tấn công Mã d7.
So sánh việc bắt Mã bằng Hậu với việc dùng Xe bắt ngay.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White starts 270 cp down nominally and both kings face threats. Qd6+ attacks king c7 and knight d7; check denies Black a free turn, and Qxd7+ wins a knight while keeping tempo. Rd1 supports the queen on d7. Without the checking fork, ordinary rook capture does not achieve the goal.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 41 legal roots compared, including checks and quiet moves. No immediate safe gain or positive mating lead. Rxd7+ Kxd7 loses the exchange; Qb7+? Kxb7 loses the queen; Bxe5+ Nxe5 loses the bishop. Qe7 and Rc1+ have defensive resources but no simpler verified non-fork material gain. Several quiet moves lose to concrete mating replies. Direct Qxb2 is only check while Na4 still covers b2; no false claim of an immediate Qxb2# threat is made.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: There are exactly two legal replies to Qd6+: Kb7 allows Qxd7+; Kd8 allows Qxd7# (legally replayed immediate checkmate, not an engine-score assertion). The best continued defence Rc7 after Qxd7+ was reviewed; White need not win the c8 rook and keeps the knight gain. All immediate recaptures and mating counterattacks checked; no sacrifice offers. Do not call Kb7 forced.
reviewNotes.level: A: two solver moves, direct queen checking fork followed by knight capture. The kingside context adds a concrete tempo decision without requiring extra preparation or a sacrifice. The objective remains winning material; the worse defence allowing mate does not change it to a forced-mate exercise.
reviewNotes.provenance: Exact complete TWIC1663 game/FEN/source ply and preceding move legally replayed. Qd6+ Kb7 Qxd7+ Rc7 was played. Official FIDE profile https://ratings.fide.com/profile/25092340 verifies Nihal Sarin25092340, GM since2018 (also IM2017), matching the master identity in the source headers. Checksummed archive reference retained.

reviews.reason: The attacked queen escapes with check and forks the rook, turning a material deficit into a concrete gain. Queen interposition is also tested.
reviews.distinctness: The essential extra decision is to move the queen out of the opposing queen b2 attack with tempo: Qd3+ simultaneously escapes attack and forks king b1/rook f1. The non-king defence Qc2 must also be considered. Unlike existing Frilles Qh4+/Qxe1, the queen is already under attack and must preserve its initiative while evading the exchange; it is not merely a shifted king/rook fork.
reviews.solutionVi: Qd3+ đưa Hậu ra khỏi đường tấn công của Hậu trắng ở b2, đồng thời chiếu Vua b1 và tấn công Xe f1. Sau Ka2, Qxf1 thu Xe. Nếu Trắng che chiếu bằng Qc2, Qxf1+ vẫn thắng Xe.
hintsVi: Hậu đen đang bị tấn công. Tìm nước vừa tránh đổi Hậu, vừa chiếu và tấn công Xe.
Kiểm tra cả khả năng Trắng dùng Hậu che chiếu.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black is 300 cp down nominally, and Qb2 attacks Qd4 along b2-c3-d4. Qd3+ escapes that attack while creating simultaneous king-b1/rook-f1 threats. Taking the rook gains500 nominal cp from the source position, reversing the material deficit. The queen had no direct capture of f1 from d4; the checking fork creates it.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 30 legal roots compared, with immediate mates and quiet tactical continuations included. Qd3+ is the only positive finite root; many ordinary queen/king/pawn moves allow a mating attack. Qxb2+ loses the queen in the reviewed line; no simpler safe capture or non-fork two-solver-move material route was found, and there are no unresolved shortcut searches.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All four legal replies covered: Ka2 gives Qxf1, Kc1/Ka1/Qc2 give Qxf1+. In particular Qc2 interposes the attacked white queen but does not save the rook. Reviewed strong continuation Qc3 after capture and alternatives Qh2/Qa3, with no immediate material recovery or mating refutation and continued positive searched assessment. No non-recovered sacrifice offers. Ka2 is an example, not forced.
reviewNotes.level: A: the queen move and rook capture are the two solver moves. Evading the attacked queen with check is direct use of tempo, with no preparatory sacrifice or long calculation.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete TWIC1663 original game, archive checksum, exact FEN/ply and preceding move match. Qd3+ Ka2 Qxf1 was actually played. Official FIDE profile https://ratings.fide.com/profile/11100516 verifies solver Justin Blackman11100516, FIDE Master since2018, matching J Blackman in the game headers; no reliance on rating alone.

reviews.reason: Bxc6 removes the c6 blocker by an ordinary minor-piece exchange; after the strongest bxc6, Nxc6 forks Queen e7 and Rook d8. The exchange gain survives Qxd8 and every legal reply to the fork has a checked material payoff.
reviews.distinctness: A non-checking Knight fork of Queen and Rook, prepared by replacing a Knight blocker with a pawn and capturing that pawn. Unlike the existing B knight checks, the defender can move either major target, and the learner must choose the remaining one.
reviews.solutionVi: Bxc6 đổi Tượng lấy Mã để dọn ô c6. Sau ...bxc6, Nxc6 tấn công đồng thời Hậu e7 và Xe d8. Trong phương án minh họa ...Qe8 Nxd8 Qxd8, Trắng đổi Mã lấy Xe và thu lợi vật chất. Đen đã chơi ...Qd6 trong ván đấu; phương án ...Qe8 là phân tích.
hintsVi: Chưa vội dùng Mã bắt quân ở c6. Hãy đổi quân đang chiếm ô này trước.
Sau khi Tốt b7 bắt lại ở c6, Mã e5 có thể tạo hai mối đe dọa nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Direct Nxc6 is answered bxc6 and does not win the exchange. Bxc6 bxc6 replaces the blocker so Nxc6 creates the Queen/Rook fork; it is not a free initial capture.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Reviewed every legal root, immediate mates, checks and captures. Only Bxc6 is materially winning in the full-root comparison; Nxc6 is -49 cp and e3 about equal. No independent simpler gain or mate appears.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After Bxc6 the strongest defence is bxc6. Declining recapture leaves the c6 Knight lost; Nd5 Bxd5 exd5 also leaves a net minor-piece gain. All 32 replies after Nxc6 have a verified target capture surviving immediate recovery. Nxd8 Qxd8 wins the exchange, not an intact Rook.
reviewNotes.level: Three solver moves with one ordinary B-for-N exchange and no sacrifice; neither moving attacker nor relevant blocker is offered uncompensated. A short, explicit preparation fits B.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete legal source game and exact ply/preceding Rd8 retained from checksummed TWIC1663 archive. FIDE profile https://ratings.fide.com/profile/8703884 confirms Hampus Sorensen, IM since2021. Actual game chose Qd6, not the sample Qe8.

reviews.reason: Rh6+ draws the exposed King to f5 with tempo; Nd6+ then forks that King and Rook e8. The material gain survives Rxe8 and needs no speculative promotion claim.
reviews.distinctness: Rook check relocates the enemy King onto a Knight-fork square while the Knight is also needed to protect the checking Rook. This differs from the existing queen checks that prepare a Knight fork; the advanced f6 pawn gives meaningful endgame counterplay without being the worksheet objective.
reviews.solutionVi: Rh6+ đưa Vua đen đến f5. Tiếp theo, Nd6+ đồng thời chiếu Vua f5 và tấn công Xe e8. Sau ...Kg4 Nxe8 Rxe8, Trắng đổi Mã lấy Xe, thu lợi vật chất; Tốt f6 vẫn tạo sức ép phong cấp. Phương án này đã xuất hiện trong ván đấu.
hintsVi: Tìm nước chiếu bằng Xe để đưa Vua đen vào tầm tấn công của Mã.
Sau khi Vua đến f5, ô nào giúp Mã đồng thời chiếu Vua và tấn công Xe?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White is about70 cp down in nominal material. Rh6+ is protected by Nf7 and forces Kf5; then Nd6+ creates the essential King/Rook fork. Direct Nd6 lacks the tempo and is losing in the root comparison.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Every legal root was compared; Rh6+ is the only positive root, at+533 cp, while direct Nd6 and routine pawn/rook moves lose. No short mate, immediate safe capture or simpler material route survives.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Only Kf5 answers Rh6+, and only Kg4 answers Nd6+. Nxe8 gains a Rook but Rxe8 returns the Knight; the retained exchange gain is180 nominal cp from the start. Strong engine continuations continue through Rxe8 and f7; the claim remains material gain, not automatic promotion or game win.
reviewNotes.level: Exactly three solver moves, one forcing relocation and a direct Knight fork. Rh6 is protected by Nf7, so this is not a Rook sacrifice. Capturing e8 is an ordinary exchange gain even when the Knight is recaptured.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete source game, exact FEN/source ply and preceding move retained from checksummed TWIC1664. Main five-ply solution matches actual play. FIDE https://ratings.fide.com/profile/2106388 identifies Luis Paulo Supi, GM since2018; the PGN also reports the opponent as IM.

reviews.reason: The equal Rook exchange draws the Bishop from e3 to c1, where Qe1+ attacks King and Bishop on the first rank. Qxc1 is a genuine extra Bishop after the equal exchange, with relevant pawn recovery checked.
reviews.distinctness: An equal Rook exchange places a Bishop on the Queen fork line. Unlike the existing B queen forks after checks or removal of a minor attacker, the preparatory recapture changes the target piece location and exposes a rank double attack.
reviews.solutionVi: ...Rxc1+ đổi Xe và đưa Tượng trắng đến c1 sau Bxc1. Khi đó ...Qe1+ đồng thời chiếu Vua g1 và tấn công Tượng c1. Sau Kg2, ...Qxc1 thu Tượng. Trắng có thể bắt Tốt d5, nhưng Đen vẫn hơn vật chất so với thế cờ ban đầu. Phương án này đã được chơi trong ván đấu.
hintsVi: Nếu Trắng dùng Tượng bắt lại Xe ở c1, Hậu đen có thể khai thác vị trí mới của Tượng như thế nào?
Sau Bxc1, Hậu có nước chiếu nào đồng thời tấn công Tượng trên hàng ngang thứ nhất?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Initial material is equal. Rxc1+ Bxc1 is an equal Rook exchange, not an upfront gain; Qe1+ then forks Kg1 and Bc1. Direct Qxe3 fails tactically and ordinary Rook/Queen moves do not win comparable material.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Every legal root, checks and captures reviewed. Rxc1+ is+492 cp; next-best Rc4 is only+54 cp. No competing immediate mate or simple material-winning root appears. A line after Qd1 can mate, but that is an inferior defensive branch, not a mate from the starting position.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All three legal responses to Rxc1+ inspected: Bxc1 is strongest; Kg2 leaves an extra Rook and Qd1 loses to Rxd1+. After Bxc1 Qe1+ only Kg2 is legal, so Qxc1 wins the Bishop. Qxd5 gives back one pawn; bounded defensive PVs continue through later pawn collection and retain a clear gain.
reviewNotes.level: One ordinary Rook exchange prepares a direct Queen fork, completed in three solver moves. No uncompensated offer or extra preparation is required, so B fits.
reviewNotes.provenance: Exact source game/FEN/preceding move retained from checksummed TWIC1663. Main sequence matches actual play. FIDE https://ratings.fide.com/profile/5203791 identifies John Ranel Morazo as FM since2024, consistent with the PGN BlackFideId and title.

reviews.reason: Kxd4 takes a central pawn before White can exchange g7 for it; following Rxg7, Rf2+ forks King c2 and pawn h2 so Black retains a genuine extra pawn. The motif is the answer to the immediate material recovery, not an incidental check.
reviews.distinctness: King capture first accounts for the opponent Rook capturing a remote pawn; the Rook fork then preserves the net gain. This adds a different preparation and material-accounting decision from Cheng–Shabalov’s Rook exchanges on f2, despite the shared final checking rank.
reviews.solutionVi: ...Kxd4 bắt Tốt d4. Trắng có thể đáp Rxg7 để lấy lại một Tốt, nhưng ...Rf2+ đồng thời chiếu Vua c2 và tấn công Tốt h2. Sau Kb1, ...Rxh2 giúp Đen thu thêm một Tốt so với thế cờ ban đầu. Đây là phương án đã được chơi; Trắng cũng có thể chọn các nước Xe khác.
hintsVi: Tính nước bắt Tốt bằng Vua, rồi kiểm tra khả năng Trắng bắt Tốt g7.
Sau Rxg7, Xe đen có thể vừa chiếu Vua vừa tấn công Tốt nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black starts only one pawn ahead, with active opposing Rook counterplay. Kxd4 alone is neutralized in material by Rxg7. Rf2+ creates competing King/h2 threats and restores the net pawn gain; without that fork the captured d4 pawn does not by itself establish the claimed extra material.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Every legal root was reviewed, including Kd5 and immediate Rook checks. Kxd4 is the top root+411 cp; Kd5+291 cp is an endgame continuation without a demonstrated simpler net material win in the stated short horizon. No short mate or safe immediate material route appears.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Following Kxd4, strongest Rook replies Rxg7, Rb7 and Rd7 were reviewed. With Rxg7, all legal replies Kb1/Kc1/Kd1 to Rf2+ allow Rxh2 and survive every immediate countercapture. Against Rb7, Rf2+ wins with flexible King activity (Kb1 Kc4) rather than asserting Rxh2 is always the best continuation. The selected line retains at least a pawn of nominal gain; strong PVs continue through later counterplay.
reviewNotes.level: Three solver moves: a safe King capture, followed by a checking Rook fork and pawn capture. The sample offers neither King nor Rook; no sacrifice is needed. The task is to gain material in a contested Rook ending, not to claim a forced game win.
reviewNotes.provenance: Full source game and exact FEN/preceding move retained from checksummed TWIC1664. Main sample matches recorded play. FIDE https://ratings.fide.com/profile/101710 identifies Luis Ernesto Rodi as IM since2011; the PGN ID/title match.

reviews.reason: Bxe2 exchanges Bishops and induces Rxe2, placing a new Rook target on e2. The quiet Nc3 forks Queen a4 and that Rook; Nxe2+ Qxe2 retains the exchange gain. Declining the initial recapture leaves Black a minor piece for at most a pawn.
reviews.distinctness: The preparatory equal exchange relocates the opponent Rook onto the fork square. Unlike Sorensen’s removal of a blocking Knight followed by a capturing fork, Nc3 is a quiet fork after a target is placed; the two cases require different initial decisions and defensive accounting.
reviews.solutionVi: ...Bxe2 đổi Tượng, đưa Xe trắng đến e2 sau Rxe2. Khi đó ...Nc3 tấn công đồng thời Hậu a4 và Xe e2. Sau Qc4, ...Nxe2+ Qxe2 giúp Đen đổi Mã lấy Xe và thu lợi vật chất. Phương án này đã xuất hiện trong ván đấu.
hintsVi: Tìm phép đổi quân mà sau khi Trắng dùng Xe bắt lại, Mã có thể tấn công Xe.
Sau Rxe2, Mã d5 có thể đồng thời tấn công Hậu và Xe bằng một nước không chiếu.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Initial nominal material is equal. Bxe2 Rxe2 is an equal Bishop exchange, but it places the Rook on e2 so Nc3 can fork Qa4 and Re2. Direct Knight moves do not establish the same gain; the fork is the mechanism of the extra exchange.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Every legal starting move was compared, including captures, checks and quiet moves. Bxe2 is the only positive root at+331 cp; next best Bb5 is negative. No immediate mate, direct safe capture or simpler independent material route appears.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rxe2 is strongest after Bxe2. Qxc6 instead concedes a Bishop for a pawn and Bd3 saves the capturing Bishop; Qa3 also leaves the captured Bishop lost. After Rxe2 Nc3, every legal reply has checked Queen/Rook target capture and immediate material-recovery coverage. On Qc4 Nxe2+ Qxe2, Black retains a Rook-for-Knight gain of180 nominal cp; deeper defensive PVs preserve the gain.
reviewNotes.level: Three solver moves with one normal Bishop exchange and one quiet Knight fork. The attacker is not sacrificed: the final recapture trades Knight for Rook with a durable gain. The short target-placement preparation fits B.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete legal game, exact starting FEN/source ply and preceding move retained from checksummed TWIC1664 archive. The complete main line matches actual play. The organizer/arbiter’s official Olympiad results identify Ezio Righi, FIDE ID11800038, as FM, matching PGN WhiteFideId/WhiteTitle: https://s4.chess-results.com/tnrWZ.aspx?art=9&fed=PNG&fedb=BDI&flag=30&lan=1&snr=753&tno=1469895&turdet=YES . FIDE profile fetch timed out; no inferred title date is claimed.

reviews.reason: Essential five-move combination from near-balanced material: answer the check by exchanging bishops, give up both rooks for the queen and king displacement, then use the queen fork to win back the rook. The pre-fork exchange itself loses100cp, so the final fork creates the gain.
reviews.distinctness: Adds a check-evasion decision and a two-rooks-for-queen transaction culminating in a queen fork. The first rook check threatens Qb2 if declined; the second rook recapture invites the king onto e2, the exact square needed for Qe4+/Qxd5. Compared with all18 active D positions, this differs from the Movsesian–Bhat repeated single-rook/knight-fork sequence and Jobava–Gaponenko queen recapture line: here both rooks disappear, the queen changes targets through the newly opened e4 square, and the exchange is only profitable after the final king/rook fork.
reviews.solutionVi: Bxd5 đáp chiếu và đổi Tượng. Sau Rxd5, Re2+ Qxe2 Rxe2+ Kxe2, Đen đổi hai Xe lấy Hậu và kéo Vua trắng đến e2. Qe4+ vừa chiếu Vua vừa tấn công Xe d5; sau Kf2, Qxd5 thu Xe. Trắng có thể bắt Tốt h4 bằng Nxh4, nhưng Đen vẫn thu lợi về vật chất.
hintsVi: Trước hết xử lý nước chiếu. Sau khi đổi Tượng, tìm nước chiếu bằng Xe trên cột e.
Tính đủ các lần bắt lại ở e2, rồi tìm nước chiếu của Hậu đồng thời tấn công Xe d5.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Initial nominal balance is -50cp for Black. Bxd5 answers the bishop check and exchanges bishops after Rxd5. Re2+ threatens the white queen on b2 while checking Kf2; Qxe2 Rxe2+ Kxe2 trades two500cp rooks for a900cp queen, a100cp deficit, not a completed material win. Qe4+ then newly attacks king e2 and rook d5 (also Nf3/Pb4), and Qxd5 creates a400cp gain versus start. Thus the final fork, not merely an unrelated favorable exchange, supplies the payoff.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All five legal starting check evasions were compared. Bxd5 is the only positive root (about+586cp); Kh8,Kh7,R8e6,R4e6 are negative. No immediate safe material capture, mate in two, positive root-mate lead, or verified two-solver-move shortcut exists. The checking context forbids ignoring Bd5 with a routine capture elsewhere. reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Starting nominal Black balance is +70cp, a meaningful material contest with White Qd5, an advanced protected d6 pawn, two ways to capture Ne5, and an exposed Black King. reviews.reason: Rff7 doubles the rook pressure and the strongest Rxc7 defence allows the bishop recapture to fork king and pawn. The pawn remains won after the recapture sequence.
reviews.distinctness: The existing B bishop example Ba4–Bxc6+ relocates the bishop to create the threat. Here the bishop waits on a5 while a second rook doubles on the seventh rank and provokes a rook exchange. The learner must see that the recapture both restores material and gives a tempo to capture d6.
reviews.solutionVi: Rff7 đưa Xe thứ hai lên hàng 7, tăng sức ép lên Tượng g7. Trong ván đấu, Đen đáp Rxc7 và Trắng bắt lại bằng Bxc7+. Tượng c7 vừa chiếu Vua b8, vừa tấn công Tốt d6. Sau Kc8, Bxd6 thắng một Tốt.
hintsVi: Tìm cách tăng sức ép của hai Xe trên hàng 7.

Sau khi Vua đen tránh chiếu, xem Tượng c7 còn tấn công quân nào.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rff7 increases pressure on the guarded g7 bishop. After Rxc7 the equal Bxc7+ recapture is simultaneously a new check and attack on d6. The capture on d6 is the incremental gain; the rook exchange itself is materially equal.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 39 roots checked, with no immediate gain or mate and no recorded short bypass. Targeted 1m MultiPV checks on Rxa7 and Bf7 show Kxa7 and Rh8 respectively maintain material balance through the short horizon. Rf7+ in the Rxa7 line hits guarded pieces and its ensuing positional edge is not a comparable short material win.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rxc7 is the strongest defence in both supplied preparation searches. After Bxc7+, Kc8 and Ka8 allow Bxd6; Kb7 and Ka7 allow Bxd6+. No immediate recapture cancels the pawn. Stronger concessions after Nd7 allow Rxa7 Kxa7 Rxd7+ and +320 net; after Ng6 the analysed rook attack also retains the advantage. These alternatives do not force the sample.
reviewNotes.level: One quiet preparatory doubling move, ordinary rook exchange and two short payoff moves. The material is +110 at start and +210 after Bxd6, a +100 gain. No offered-material flag or genuine sacrifice.

reviews.reason: Qb8+ forces the king onto the knight’s checking fork. Both king retreats allow Nxe6+ for one pawn, and moving the knight off f8 reopens the queen’s line to prevent a counterattack.
reviews.distinctness: Kasparov–Shirov also uses a queen check to enable a knight fork. Here the queen remains on the eighth rank and the knight briefly blocks its line on f8. The pawn capture opens that line with discovered check against either king retreat, a concrete extra decision that preserves the move tempo against the queen on c3. Separate these positions in order.
reviews.solutionVi: Qb8+ chiếu dọc hàng 8 và buộc Vua đen xuống h7. Nf8+ tấn công đôi Vua h7 và Tốt e6. Dù Vua về g8 như trong ván đấu hay về h8, Nxe6+ đều thắng một Tốt. Khi Mã rời f8 để bắt Tốt, Hậu b8 lại chiếu dọc hàng 8, buộc Đen tiếp tục đỡ chiếu.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Nf8 is not check against the initial king on g8. Qb8+ forces Kh7 and creates that target. Nf8+ attacks the king and e6. Nxe6+ then reopens the b8 queen’s line against either retreat, keeping Black from taking time for a counterattack.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 40 roots checked. Qb8+ leads the supplied root comparison. At one million nodes Qf8+ Kh7 Rf1 Qxd4 Qxf7 merely restores the initial balance; Rf1 Ra8 delays a net pawn beyond three solver moves; Re3 Qa1+ holds the initial balance within the horizon. Rb1’s supplied stronger defence does not give a short comparable gain. After Qb8+ Kh7, Nf8+ clearly leads at one million nodes.

reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 31 roots checked, no immediate gain or short mate. The next strongest Bd8 and Bxc5 hold no engine advantage, and neither establishes the short payoff. reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The supplied prep searches alternate g3 and g4 as best and show the same protected g3 idea. Against g3, Qxg3+ immediately recovers a pawn with check and the bishop prevents Kxg3. Against g4, Qg3+ Kh1 Qxh3+ has no cancelling recapture. Kg1 permits Qxg4+; the solution states only the immediate +100. Qf2 is a weaker concession and no mate claim is made.
reviewNotes.level: One quiet move supports the entry and permits the three-move non-sacrificial fork sequence. Black starts down one pawn and the sample restores material equality, an incremental one-pawn gain.

Existing B rook examples use king movement or a preparatory rook exchange rather than attacking the defender of the entry square.

Nếu Đen chọn Nc8 thay cho Nf5, Trắng vẫn bắt được Tốt b7 bằng Rxb7+. Sau Ka8, Mã c8 còn giữ a7, nên Trắng có thể chơi Rhg7 để tiếp tục bảo vệ Xe b7 và giữ lợi thế một Tốt.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: An immediate Rxb7+ loses to Nxb7. A recapture Rxb7+ then allows Kxb7. Rcd7 attacks Nd6, which guards b7, before the rook invades with check. The two rooks protect each other and Rxb7+ attacks a7 while Black must answer check.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 24 roots compared. Direct Rxb7+ is refuted by Nxb7 in a one-million-node check. The leading Kd1 alternative meets Rd8 with no short material gain, and Kd2 and Rce7 still use Rcd7 in the supplied continuations. None supplies a shorter equivalent safe payoff.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The one-million-node search ranks Nc8, e5, Nc4, Ne4 and Rg8 among strong replies. Nc8 makes Ka8 the only reply to Rxb7+ and defends a7, so Rhg7 safely holds the first pawn and keeps b7 supported. Nc4 and Ne4 yield the same checking entry; after Nc4 and Kc8, Rhc7+ maintains coordination. Rg8 leaves the knight capturable on d6. In the played branch Rxb7+ has Ka8 and Kc8 only; after Kc8, Rxa7 also retains +200. After the played Ka8 Rxa7+ only Kb8 is legal, with no cancelling capture.
reviewNotes.level: Initial material -20 cp. One quiet rook preparation attacks a defender; checking entry and pawn capture give +200 cp in the played line. The best defence still concedes +100 cp at the checking entry. No offer or sacrifice.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete TWIC 1663 Olympiad game replayed at ply 60; all five sample plies were played. Source archive checksum matches corpus manifest. FIDE confirms Wong Ho Cheung’s FM title since 2014 https://ratings.fide.com/profile/6001394.

reviews.reason: Quiet Qd3 creates a checking pawn-capture threat. When Kf2 guards g3, Qc2+ creates the necessary King/Rook fork. All five defences permit Qxa4 and the played branch retains a Rook gain through relevant counterplay.
reviews.distinctness: Compared with the 20 active B records, including Blackburne–Hanson and Baninga–Morazo. Those prepare a Queen fork by a capture or exchange. This uses a quiet Queen route from a6 to d3, threatens a checking pawn capture, and exploits the King’s move to protect that pawn. It teaches switching from one threat to a fork when the opponent defends, unlike Zaw–Kandil’s pawn-supported intermediate Rook check and the reserve’s sacrificed Knight.
reviews.solutionVi: …Qd3 đe dọa bắt Tốt g3 có chiếu. Sau Kf2, Vua trắng đã bảo vệ Tốt g3, nhưng …Qc2+ vừa chiếu Vua vừa tấn công Xe a4. Trong ván đấu, Trắng dùng Re2 đỡ chiếu, rồi …Qxa4 thu Xe. Nếu Vua chọn một ô tránh chiếu, Đen vẫn bắt được Xe a4.
hintsVi: Tìm một nước Hậu không chiếu nhưng đe dọa bắt Tốt g3 có chiếu.
Sau Kf2, nếu Hậu bắt Tốt g3 thì Vua trắng có thể bắt lại. Tìm một nước chiếu khác tấn công cả Xe a4.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: At the +100cp nominal start, Black cannot capture Ra4 from a6 because its own a5 pawn blocks the file. Qd3 reroutes the Queen and creates a real Qxg3+ threat. Kf2 protects g3, as Qxg3+ Kxg3 confirms, and puts the King on the second rank. Qc2+ now checks Kf2 and attacks Ra4 along c2–b3–a4. The Rook gain depends on this fork.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Compared all 33 roots and legally replayed their bounded PVs. No immediate safe gain, local two-solver shortcut, or forced short mate. Rxd4 Rxd4 cxd4 exchanges a Rook for a pawn and is unsuitable. Root cxd4 permits h5 counterplay, and R8d6 and Kf7 lead to longer positional play. The exact local second-move capture scan after Qd3 found no safe capture after Kf2. At matched 1.5m restricted roots after Kf2, Qxc3 +273 and Qc2+ +540. The legal Qxc3 h5 Qc2+ Kf3 Kf7 Qg6+ Kf8 Rxe6 line gives back the nominal pawn before regaining later. This substantiates the absence of a comparably safe capture bypass in the taught branch. Ra2 does allow other material threats, including Qxg3+, as expected when White protects a different target.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Qd3 was compared with all 30 immediate replies and top defences were examined. At 1.5m MultiPV7, Ra2 and Rxe6+ are strongest. Rxe6+ Kxe6 Qg6+ Ke7 Qxg7+ Kd6 Rxa5 leaves Black +200cp versus start, and later Qf6+ R5d6 Rxc5+ still leaves +100cp before Qxg3+. Ra2 permits Qxc3 Rae2 Qxg3+ and further gains or the packet’s Qxg3+ Rg2 Qxe1+. Rxa5 uses another counterplay route. The selected Kf2 branch is played, not called forced. After Qc2+ each legal Kf3, Ke3, Kg1, Kf1 and Re2 allows Qxa4. Sample gains +500cp, no immediate recapture, and immediate counterchecks/captures still leave at least +400cp. The exact 1m h5 Qe8 continuation retains at least +500cp in the strongest reviewed line. This is a material claim after relevant recovery, not a game-win or exhaustive forcing claim.
reviewNotes.level: One quiet non-sacrificial preparation, then a checking Queen fork and a third-move capture. Qd3 releases its own a5 pawn, but Rxa5 Qxg3+ immediately trades it for g3 and all immediate replies keep the balance. The remaining listed captures concern pawns still defendable or White’s Rook offer Rxe6+, which Black recaptures with Kxe6. The played five-ply line fits B short coordination.

reviews.reason: Qe8+ drives the king from d8 to c7, where Qc6+ checks and attacks three pawns. Both king retreats concede d6. The other two pawns are guarded, so the target choice matters.
reviews.distinctness: Kasparov–Beliavsky uses a related two-check queen maneuver and has just one king reply to each check. Here learners compare both possible retreats after Qc6+ and distinguish the exposed d6 pawn from the b6 and c5 pawns, each defended by a different piece. Place apart from Kasparov–Beliavsky.
reviews.solutionVi: Qe8+ buộc Vua đen rời d8 đến c7. Tốt d5 bảo vệ ô c6, nên Trắng có thể chơi Qc6+, vừa chiếu Vua vừa tấn công các Tốt b6, c5 và d6. Xe a6 giữ Tốt b6, còn Tốt b6 giữ Tốt c5. Dù Vua lui về d8 như trong ván đấu hay về b8, Qxd6+ đều thắng một Tốt.
hintsVi: Tìm nước chiếu buộc Vua đen rời d8. Tượng h5 đang bảo vệ ô nào?
Sau Kc7, Hậu có thể chiếu từ ô nào được Tốt d5 bảo vệ?
Xét cả hai ô Vua có thể lui về. Trong ba Tốt Hậu đang tấn công, Tốt nào có thể bắt mà Đen không bắt lại được?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The bishop supports Qe8+, which forces Kc7 and removes the king from d8. The d5 pawn protects Qc6+, creating the check and attacks on b6, c5 and d6. The a6 rook and b6 pawn defend b6 and c5 respectively, so d6 is the material payoff.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 33 roots compared; Qe8+ scored +253, next g4 +24, and no immediate safe gain or mate appeared. At one million nodes after Kc7, Qc6+ is distinctly stronger than Qe7+ and Qf7+, which allow Bd7. No comparable simpler route.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kc7 is the only legal reply to Qe8+. Kd8 and Kb8 are the only legal replies to Qc6+. Both allow Qxd6+ for +100 at one million nodes. After Kd8 the legal blocks Bd7 and Qd7 do not recapture; after Kb8 the legal king moves Ka8, Kb7 and Ka7 do not recapture. Taking b6 or c5 allows Rxb6 or bxc5 respectively under either king retreat.
reviewNotes.level: One non-sacrificial checking preparation, a protected fork and a material capture. Balanced starting material and +100 after the forced defensive choices; no offer or equal exchange needed.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete TWIC 1667 FISU World University Classical game replayed to ply 60, with all five sample plies matching game play. Archive checksum matches corpus manifest. FIDE confirms Stalmach’s IM title since 2023 https://ratings.fide.com/profile/372048.

reviews.reason: A quiet pawn advance both supports the checking Rook entry and opens the Bishop line to c2. The opponent’s strongest reply takes the Bishop, and the checking fork wins one pawn before completing an equal Bishop exchange. The material remains after the immediate replies and a reviewed rook-ending continuation.
reviews.distinctness: Compared with all 20 active B records. Eltag–Rodi d3f989771c8a877c and Cheng–Shabalov 697208e5569635d9 use a Rook fork on the second rank, but their preparation uses a King capture or Rook exchange. Here the pinned f2 pawn cannot take e3 and the quiet pawn simultaneously guards the Rook entry and clears Bf5–c2. The temporary Bishop capture is settled by a checking intermediate fork. It is also distinct from the other packet’s Knight reroute and Queen preparations.
reviews.solutionVi: …e3 bảo vệ ô f2 và mở đường chéo của Tượng f5 đến c2. Tốt trắng f2 không thể bắt sang e3 vì sẽ để Xe d2 chiếu Vua. Sau Bxf5, …Rxf2+ là nước chiếu xen giữa, đồng thời tấn công Tượng f5. Trong ván đấu, Vua tránh chiếu bằng Kg3, rồi …Rxf5 bắt lại Tượng. Hai bên đổi Tượng và Đen thu thêm Tốt f2.
hintsVi: Thử …Rxf2+ ngay. Vua trắng có bắt được Xe ở f2 không?
Tìm cách bảo vệ f2 bằng Tốt e. Vì sao Tốt trắng f2 không thể bắt sang e3?
Sau Bxf5, hãy dùng một nước chiếu để lấy Tốt trước khi bắt lại Tượng.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: At the equal-material start, direct Rxf2+ Kxf2 loses the Rook. e3 supports f2, and the f2 pawn cannot play fxe3 because it is pinned by Rd2 to Kg2. e3 also opens Bf5–c2. White Bxf5 removes the Bishop along the cleared diagonal, and Rxf2+ attacks Kg2 and the Bishop f5 with the same Rook. All four King moves allow Rxf5. The intermediate fork creates the pawn gain while completing the equal Bishop exchange.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Reviewed all 27 roots. No mate or short safe alternative. Rxf2+ Kxf2 is directly refuted, and Rxc2 Rxc2 loses a Rook for Bishop because e4 blocks Black Bf5 from c2. e3 addresses both exact obstacles. Kg7, f6, Be6 and b5 give no comparably clear material gain in the recorded branches.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All immediate replies considered. Supplemental 1m MultiPV8 has Bxf5 as strongest. After e3, retreats Bb1/Bb3/Ba4 allow Rxb2, while Kg3/Kf3 or b4 leave the c2 Bishop to the now-supported Rxc2 Rxc2 Bxc2. g6 similarly permits Bxc2 and h7 recapture. These are weaker responses, so Bxf5 leads the exercise. Rxf2+ has Kh3, Kg3, Kh1 and Kg1, each allowing Rxf5 with no immediate recapture. Sample net +100cp. The 1m h4 probe identifies f6 Re1 fxg5 Rxe3 gxh4+ Kxh4 Kf7 and holds +100cp across the reviewed continuation. Other Black choices can return a pawn, so the solution claims the demonstrated material gain only.
reviewNotes.level: One quiet pawn preparation, a forcing Rook fork and a third-move recapture. White temporarily takes the f5 Bishop but cannot avoid losing its Bishop in the main branch after the checking intermediate move. This is a favorable equal Bishop exchange plus a pawn, with no genuine sacrifice.

reviews.reason: Qf8 creates a concrete threat on h6. The Knight blocks the supporting Rook and becomes the target of the subsequent Queen fork.
reviews.distinctness: A quiet threat forces the learner to see how an interposing defender becomes a fork target. The preparation differs from the existing Queen-check king drives and capture exchanges.
reviews.solutionVi: Qf8 dọa bắt Tốt h6 chiếu hết nhờ Xe h8 bảo vệ ô h6. Trong ván đấu, ...Nh7 chặn đường Xe. Trắng chơi Qg8+, vừa chiếu Vua g6 vừa tấn công Mã h7. Sau ...Kf6, Qxh7 bắt Mã mà Đen không thể bắt lại ngay.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Qf8 threatens Qxh6# if the threat is ignored, as confirmed by a legal threat replay. Nh7 cuts Rh8’s protection of h6 and exposes the Knight to Qg8+.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Qf8 is the only positive root in the bounded complete root comparison. Direct forcing checks and captures do not establish a shorter gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The strongest examined preparation reply is Nh7. Against Rh5 White can capture with Nxh5 and meet the counterattack. Ng8 allows Rxg8+. After Qg8+, Kf6 is the only legal reply and Qxh7 has no immediate recapture.
reviewNotes.level: Three White moves and one non-sacrificial preparation. The pawn-on-h6 mating threat is conditional. The exercise objective is winning material.

reviews.reason: The rook check leaves Kf2 as the sole reply. That places the king on the Knight’s attacking square, so the Queen is won with tempo.
reviews.distinctness: A forced rook-file check sets up a King–Queen fork while Black starts an exchange down. The payoff is a queen without recapture, unlike the existing king-cage rook captures.
reviews.solutionVi: ...Rc1+ buộc Vua trắng đến f2. Từ e3, Mã đen nhảy đến g4, chiếu Vua f2 và tấn công Hậu f6. Sau nước đỡ chiếu, Đen bắt Hậu bằng ...Nxf6. Trong ván đấu, Trắng chọn Ke2.
hintsVi: Xe nào có thể chiếu để đưa Vua trắng tới một ô Mã có thể tấn công?
Từ g4, Mã tấn công đồng thời ô f2 và ô nào có Hậu trắng?

reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Complete root comparison has no two-move material shortcut. Rd1+ is another preparation for the same Knight fork, so the sample is one solution.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kf2 is the sole reply after Rc1+. After Ng4+, Ke2, Kf3 and Kg3 all allow Nxf6; no immediate recapture removes the Queen gain. Rf5 pressures the Knight afterwards but the sampled continuation keeps the material.
reviewNotes.level: Three Black moves, no sacrifice or extended preparatory calculation.

exclusions.reason: Incidental final pawn fork: Qxf6 gxf6 d8=Q+ has already gained230cp against both legal king replies before Qxa5. The named fork is unnecessary to the stated material gain; the longer Qd5/Kh3/Qd6 teaching preparation also exceeds the shorter actually played Qf7 route.
exclusions.distinctness: Promotion is the real winning mechanism, already restoring the queen and winning bishop-for-pawn material. Adding a king/pawn fork to collect a5 supplies no necessary new defensive decision for Fork D. Keep as a possible promotion lead outside this fork batch; no claim that its source or whole game is invalid.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Starting nominal material is +70cp. After sample Qxf6 gxf6 d8=Q+, White has already gained230cp: queen exchanged for bishop, then queen restored by promotion. Both legal replies Kg7 and Kh7 preserve that gain. Qxa5 merely adds a pawn; the final king-and-pawn fork is incidental rather than essential to winning material.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All33 legal starting moves were compared. Qc8+ is at least as strong in bounded analysis, and the full original game uses the shorter d7 Be7 Qf7 Bf6 Qxf6 Rxf6 d8=Q+ Kh7 Qxa5 route. The actual source move is Qf7, not Qg7. The sample delays the same promotion payoff with extra queen/king moves; no need to resolve a forced mate or deeper shortcut because the exercise already fails motif necessity.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The queen sacrifice is a genuine accepted material cost of570cp, with promotion compensation correctly distinguished from an ordinary exchange. Legal reply/recovery review confirms the promotion payoff against both kings moves. Strong declinations and rook blocks also lead to promotion/capture material witnesses. These validate a promotion lesson, not the necessity of the final pawn fork.
reviewNotes.level: Thirteen plies/seven solver moves and a queen sacrifice do not by themselves establish an advanced fork exercise. Much of the extra coordination serves promotion; the required named-motif complexity is absent. Do not publish or pad D with this candidate.
reviewNotes.provenance: Exact complete TWIC1663 game, source FEN, previous move and archive checksum match. Headers report Begmuratov GM and Mao FM, but no independent title lookup was needed after editorial rejection. The saved teaching sample differs from actual play; retaining the complete game does not make the longer sample a played continuation.

exclusions.reason: The advertised bishop king/queen fork is a discovered rook check, not a king attacked by the bishop. Bc5+ uncovers Rd5 checking Kd2 while the bishop attacks Qf8; its extra f2-pawn attack is incidental. Material is won because the discovered check prevents the queen from escaping.
exclusions.distinctness: This is a suitable cross-topic discovery lead, not a new essential fork mechanism. It would repeat the mistake of accepting any geometric two-target attack while a separate checking line supplies the whole payoff. The 18 active D positions and three new approved combinations do not justify adding a position whose decisive forcing mechanism belongs to a different topic.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Independently replayed Qxd2+: the captured piece is the white BISHOP on d2, not a rook. After Kxd2 Bc5+, the sole checking piece is the stationary black rook on d5, through newly cleared d4 and d3 to Kd2. The bishop on c5 attacks Qf8 and Pf2, and does not attack Kd2. White cannot move the queen because of the discovered rook check, so the queen capture payoff depends on discovery. The geometric queen/pawn bishop fork is incidental and does not establish the named motif as essential.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All four legal starting check evasions Kc7,Ka7,Nc8,Rd8 were compared. Kc7 and Ka7 are similarly strong and Nc8 has an independent tactical line; none proves an essential bishop king/queen fork. After the sampled Bf5, the packet itself gives a shorter non-sacrificial Qf3+ king/pawn-fork lead, but indefinite durability of that smaller gain was not needed to decide rejection. No mate assertion or engine score substitutes for motif review.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Actual accepted queen-for-bishop cost is570cp, recovered by Bxf8 for a330cp gain versus the start. All six legal responses to Bc5+ (Kc3,Ke2,Kc2,Ke1,Kc1,Bd3) leave Bxf8, and strong declines after Kc7 were reviewed. Those replies answer the rook check, not a check by the bishop; Bd3 blocks the d-file. The tactical payoff can be sound while editorial classification as a fork still fails. No defensive move other than the sole Kxd2 response to Qxd2+ is described as forced.
reviewNotes.level: Four solver moves, a necessary check evasion and a genuine queen sacrifice can make this an advanced discovered-attack exercise. They do not make an incidental queen/pawn fork a suitable D Fork example. Do not pad D merely because the sequence has more than three solver moves.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete legal Aronian–Dubov chess.com Speed2021 game, exact source ply91/FEN and preceding Qf8+ match the normalized game ID. The downloaded Aronian archive checksum d9fa17c7a3dab9c76627e93d00bf0c6f70dbe6deb12289b71a4c34ec4601fcc5 and retrieval2026-11-06 are retained, with the established post2010 archive-master credential. Only Kc7 was played at this frame: actual continuation was Qf7+ Nd7 Qf5 Qxf5 Bxf5; Bf5/Qxd2+/Bc5+ is teaching analysis. No extra title lookup was required after motif rejection, and no source invalidity is claimed.

exclusions.reason: Kb8 answers check, but White’s stronger Kb1 leaves the planned d2 advance without check. The sampled pawn fork depends on the weaker Nc3, and the strongest branch instead wins a pawn with Qxc2+ before a substantially different continuation.
exclusions.distinctness: The pawn fork and capture-promotion would add coverage only if the short fork were a sound response to relevant defence.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: After Kb8 Kb1 the c1 king target has moved. Nc3 permits the sample pawn fork but is unnecessary. The strongest recorded line uses Qxc2+ and avoids this fork.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All three roots checked: Kb8 is strongest, Qd7 and Rd7 are worse. The issue arises after the root, since the leading branch uses a queen check and pawn capture with the intended c1 target already absent.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kb1 ranks above Nc3 at both preparation budgets. In the played sample Rxe1 removes the promoted queen and reduces the sample increase from +1300 to +400 relative to the initial material deficit.
reviewNotes.level: The sample length and absence of a sacrifice meet the mechanical B screen, but the short fork is conditional on a weak defence. Reject at this grade and objective.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete TWIC 1663 game replayed to ply 49. All five sample plies and the subsequent Rxe1 are from the game. FIDE profiles confirm both player identities and FM titles: https://ratings.fide.com/profile/2403757 and https://ratings.fide.com/profile/6707173.

exclusions.reason: Ke2 and Ke3 both allow a comparably strong h4 defence. Rg4+ then wins the same pawn by discovered check without a second rook target.
exclusions.distinctness: The sample combines a discovered check with an incidental rook attack on g2. The same preparatory king step and discovered check win a pawn when the black bishop remains on d5, so the distinguishing double attack is dispensable.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: After Ke3 Bg2 the rook attacks g2 and h5 while the bishop gives discovered check. After Ke3 h4, Rg4+ Kh1 Rxh4 gives the same gain while the rook attacks only h4. The second target is dispensable.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All five roots compared. Kf1 and Ke2 rank above Ke3 in the supplied full-root screen. At one million nodes Ke2 h4 Rg4+ Kh1 Rxh4 retains its +100 pawn against the three strongest continuations; no double attack is required.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: One-million-node checks on Ke3 show Bg2, h4 and Bb3 as strong replies. Kg1 and Kh1 both allow Rxh5 in the sample; after h4, the gain instead comes from collecting h4. After Bb3 the discovered Rg6+ permits Rxc6. The actual +100 gain survives immediate replies.
reviewNotes.level: One quiet king preparation and three solver moves fit B mechanically. The position teaches opening a bishop line and collecting a pawn rather than needing the rook fork.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete TWIC 1664 Olympiad game replayed at ply 92; all five sample plies were played. Source archive checksum matches corpus manifest. FIDE confirms Castillo Beitia’s IM title in 2026 https://ratings.fide.com/profile/6606687.

exclusions.reason: The leading g5 defence denies the checking capture on g6. Rxh6 then only restores the pawn lost on a5, and the first net gain in the leading branch comes from a later bishop capture.
exclusions.distinctness: Switching the rook between distant targets on the sixth rank would add a distinct decision if the short fork resolved the objective against strong replies. The best defence removes the checking entry.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rf6 prepares a safe checking capture on g6 after Rxa5, then the rook wins a sixth-rank pawn. After g5 the same checking fork is unavailable. The leading continuation wins by targeting a6 with the bishop after Black has first exchanged one pawn for another.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 30 roots compared. Bxg6 Rxa5 exchanges one pawn each and no short gain follows. Rd6 after Bxg6 also neutralizes the short gain; the one-million-node PV settles slightly below the initial balance. Rf6 is the strongest preparation but its leading defence changes the teaching mechanism.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The supplied searches and one-million-node five-reply search rank g5 ahead of the played Rxa5. The leading g5 line Kg2 Rxa5 Rxh6 Ra3 Bxa6 settles at +100 only on the fourth solver move. In the sample, Kf7 and Kh8 permit a pawn capture and Kf8 can lead to a sixth-rank capture with ordinary exchange. The played Rxh6 leaves +100 net after including ...Rxa5. The shortest line fails to represent the leading preparation defence.
reviewNotes.level: The played line is non-sacrificial and has three solver moves. Strongest defence pushes the net gain beyond that line and switches the payoff to a bishop capture without the rook fork.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete TWIC 1663 Olympiad game replayed at ply 82; all five sample plies were played. Source archive checksum matches corpus manifest. FIDE confirms Garzon Zapatanga’s IM title since 2025 https://ratings.fide.com/profile/3634787.

exclusions.reason: Level B excludes genuine sacrifices. Bxd7 removes the h3 Bishop’s protection of the stationary Knight on g2. The actual Bxg2 takes that Knight and leaves Black −220cp relative to the start until the later Queen fork recovers material. The automatic offer list missed this changed protection.
exclusions.distinctness: The first capture stops d8 promotion and clears the h-file for a Queen check while giving up the defender’s separate Knight duty. This is a real teaching distinction from active Blackburne–Hanson 01ee54deeca58f1a and Baninga–Morazo 34164659aebe3932, but the stationary Knight sacrifice makes this exact B record ineligible. The Meshkovs reserve Queen reroute does not lose an offered piece.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Bxd7 stops a live d7 passer and clears h3 for Qh5+. Black is −80cp nominal at the start, gains +100cp on d7, then drops to −220cp after Bxg2. Qh5+ directly checks along the h-file and attacks Rd1 on the diagonal. Qxd1+ produces +280cp versus start. The fork is essential in the accepted branch and illustrates compensation for the sacrifice.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Reviewed all 34 legal starting roots. No certified local shortcut or short forced mate for Black. Starting Qh5 is not check because Bh3 blocks the h-file and d8=Q+ is available. The point of rejecting this exact record is the necessary sacrifice, not a claim that a simpler Black solution is known.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After Bxd7, both Bxg2 and Qxg2 accept the stationary Knight offer. For example, the legal comparison Kh7 Bxg2 Bxg2+ retains an immediate Bishop recapture, while Bxd7 Bxg2 has no equivalent recovery. Qxg2+ Qxg2 Rxg2 Rxg2 simply gives White a Rook in the exchange sequence. The accepted sample stays −220cp through Qh5+. The three legal fork replies Kg1, Bh3 and Qh4 permit the local Rook gain, and Qxg2 can be answered with Qh5+ Qh2 Qxd1. Be2 instead permits a longer Bg4 attack. The evidence verifies the tactical idea but confirms the material commitment.
reviewNotes.level: Genuine unequal stationary Knight sacrifice, accepted in the source line. Bxd7 creates it by removing Bh3’s defence of g2 even though the capture geometry itself already existed. A delayed Rook gain through the fork is compensation, not an immediate equal exchange. Three solver moves do not qualify this as B.

exclusions.reason: Kh2 is the sole legal response to the initial check and makes no preparatory tactical choice. The leading b5 defence also removes b7 before Qb8+, delaying the net gain beyond the short fork.
exclusions.distinctness: The useful decision is recognizing the queen fork after Nf5. The initial forced king move adds an evasion rather than a teaching decision for Level B.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The played Qb8+ forks king and b7 after Nf5. The b5 defence vacates b7, so the same Qb8+ lacks its sample pawn target.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All roots covered; Kh2 is the only legal move, so there is no choice of preparation. After Nf5 the played queen fork is a direct decision.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: A one-million-node five-reply check identifies b5 as the leading defence. Kh2 b5 Qb8+ Kh7 Qd6 Rd1 Qf6 Kg8 Qxa6 gives a net pawn only on the fifth solver move. Nc6 also delays the direct checking fork. In the sample either Kh7 or Kg7 permits Qxb7, retaining +100.
reviewNotes.level: The five-ply sample begins with compulsory check evasion, and the best defence does not give the stated three-move gain. Reject for this Level B batch.

deferred.reason: Tactically clean local pawn gain, but not selected for this four-position expansion because its queen-check/king-retreat/pawn-capture decision repeats active Bareev–Ivanchuk and Cortes–Shabalov queen/pawn forks without a sufficiently new defensive mechanism.
deferred.distinctness: King protected h6 until displaced and both rook counterchecks matter, but the learner still makes the same direct queen check and collects a pawn as existing queen/king/pawn A exercises. Retain as an unselected lead; no tactical rejection or removal of current content.

hintsVi: Tìm nước chiếu của Hậu đồng thời tấn công một Tốt.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Qe4 does not attack h6. Qg6+ creates the king/pawn fork and king displacement permits Qxh6+. Initial nominal edge is220 cp, modest but already favorable; counterplay by both black rooks is real.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All29 roots compared. Many quiet moves retain a similar engine advantage but no direct safe capture or mate; bounded shortcut review has no unresolved or non-fork material gain. Tactical correctness is not the reason for deferral.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Both legal Kh8/Kf8 replies lose h6 without immediate recapture. Strong rook counterchecks after Qxh6+ were reviewed and do not erase the pawn in the recorded lines. No sacrifice offers; no claim of forced game win.
reviewNotes.level: A direct two-move queen fork fits the grade. It is deferred for selection variety, not relabelled to a harder level.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete checksummed TWIC1663 game and source frame/preceding move match; the three-move sample was played. Source reports FM Amir and IM Wafa; independent title confirmation was not pursued because this lead is unselected.

46bccd944e7969ac.distinctness: Adds a check-evasion decision and a two-rooks-for-queen transaction culminating in a queen fork. The first rook check threatens Qb2 if declined; the second rook recapture invites the king onto e2, the exact square needed for Qe4+/Qxd5. Compared with all18 active D positions, this differs from the Movsesian–Bhat repeated single-rook/knight-fork sequence and Jobava–Gaponenko queen recapture line: here both rooks disappear, the queen changes targets through the newly opened e4 square, and the exchange is only profitable after the final king/rook fork.

59a4bbff8800ef22.distinctness: A Rook-for-Knight offer places the opposing Rook on c7 through Queen exchanges, while a defensive ...Rd1+ must be met in between. The surviving Rook then draws the King onto the Knight-fork square. This differs from existing simple Rook decoys, repeated Queen checks and the Zukertort Queen-sacrifice Knight sequence; it adds a meaningful defensive intermezzo and target placement.

5bf5716fb3926512.distinctness: A Knight offer on c3 removes a pawn shield from the Queen diagonal c3-a1 after a checking King displacement. The opposite-wing passed pawn forces recovery planning through Qxa6/Qxa7. This is distinct from the current D Rook decoys, Queen offers and multiple Knight forks, and from Maurizzi’s Queen-exchange placement of a Rook on c7.

a3a964496ef9318a.distinctness: Compared with Karpov–Ribli’s Bishop exchange and checking Rook offer, the first move here is itself a quiet Rook fork of Queen d5/Bishop g5. More importantly, the learner must reject the tempting immediate Queen fork after the exchange and first drive the King away from the passed pawn: Qe6+ before Qf5+. This counterpromotion/King-direction decision is absent from the straightforward final Queen fork in Karpov–Ribli. The two positions therefore add different preparation and defence decisions, not just different target pieces.

48c4a54ae6c7e136.distinctness: Adds two different defensive restrictions before the sacrifice: Nf6 could take Qh5, and Nb4 could take the final Nd5 fork. Bxf6 removes the first defender and a3 forces the second off d5. The remaining knight then creates the actual king/bishop fork. Unlike existing queen- or rook-sacrifice king chases and the approved new Karpov double-rook exchange, the learner must remove two named defensive resources before sacrificing a minor piece; the final target bishop also protects h8, preventing a premature free-rook shortcut.

1b5b4544d8068285.distinctness: Adds a defensive fork combination against a mating threat and an expendable promoted queen: the original queen stays on the board, c8=Q diverts Black queen from the checking diagonal, and Rxf7+ Rxf7 both relocates the fork target and clears f5 on the d3-g6 diagonal. Unlike rejected f6d30, promotion here costs a pawn after Qxc8 rather than already yielding a material gain. Unlike active Tal/Van der Wiel or Shabalov/Mahesh Chandran promotion examples, the promoted queen is sacrificed, and the surviving original queen creates the final fork after a separate rook sacrifice.
